rationale:
The supplied proof combines two separate, reusable analytic facts, plus a short signed-to-nonnegative reduction.

(i) Portmanteau-type level-set lemma (parent step 4, with μ(C) < ∞ from step 1). For a continuous compactly supported g with tsupport g ⊆ U, hypotheses (a), (b), (c) give μ_j{g > t} → μ{g > t} for a.e. t > 0. This uses only topology (open versus compact superlevel sets) and countably many atoms of the level sets. It is child superlevel_convergence.

(ii) Layer-cake / dominated-convergence transfer (parent steps 1, 2, 3, 5). For continuous, nonnegative, compactly supported g with μ(tsupport g) < ∞, limsup_j μ_j(tsupport g) < ∞ and a.e. convergence of μ_j{g > t}, it gives ∫ g dμ_j → ∫ g dμ. It does not involve U, compacts or opens. It is child layer_cake_convergence.

Neither child uses the other; the conclusion of (i) is exactly the a.e. hypothesis of (ii).

What remains for the parent is steps 1, 2 and 6:
- f± := max(±f, 0) are continuous and nonnegative, with support ⊆ support f, so they have compact support and tsupport ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ U.
- Child (i) applies to each f±.
- (a) gives μ(tsupport f±) < ∞, and (b) followed by (a) gives limsup_j μ_j(tsupport f±) < ∞; child (ii) then gives ∫ f± dμ_j → ∫ f± dμ.
- With C = tsupport f: μ(C) < ∞, and μ_j(C) < ∞ eventually (eventually_lt_of_limsup_lt). Continuous compactly supported functions are integrable for a measure finite on C, via the finite measure ν.restrict C and integrableOn_iff_integrable_of_support_subset. So ∫ f = ∫ f⁺ − ∫ f⁻ for μ and for μ_j eventually, and Tendsto.sub plus Tendsto.congr' finish.

subproblems.title: Almost-every-level convergence of superlevel-set measures
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, and μ, μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) Borel measures on ℝ^P such that (a) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; (b) limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K ⊆ U; (c) μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G) for every open G ⊆ U (lim sup and lim inf in [0, ∞]). Let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be continuous with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ U, where tsupport g := closure{x : g(x) ≠ 0}. Then for almost every t ∈ (0, ∞) with respect to Lebesgue measure restricted to (0, ∞), μ_j({x : g(x) > t}) → μ({x : g(x) > t}) in [0, ∞] as j → ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → limsup (fun j => μs j K) atTop ≤ μ K) → (∀ G : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen G → G ⊆ U → μ G ≤ liminf (fun j => μs j G) atTop) → ∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ U → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume.restrict (Ioi (0 : ℝ))), Tendsto (fun j => μs j {x | t < g x}) atTop (𝓝 (μ {x | t < g x}))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof of `cmc_tendsto_integral_of_limsup_liminf` (the "standard approximation argument" that ends Simon's proof of 7.2.4, chapter-07.txt lines 284–289, which starts from (13) limsup_j μ_{T_j}(K) ≤ μ_T(K) for compact K ⊆ U and (14) μ_T(W) ≤ liminf_j μ_{T_j}(W) for open W ⊆ U). Here it is stated for one continuous compactly supported g. No sign condition on g is needed.
1. Notation. Let C := tsupport g = closure{x : g(x) ≠ 0}. Since g has compact support, C is compact, and C ⊆ U by hypothesis. So μ(C) < ∞ by (a).
2. The exceptional set is countable. Let μ_C := μ⌞C, i.e. μ_C(A) = μ(A ∩ C). Then μ_C(ℝ^P) = μ(C) < ∞, so μ_C is a finite measure. For s ∈ ℝ let L_s := {x : g(x) = s}. These are Borel sets, because g is continuous and hence Borel measurable, and they are pairwise disjoint for distinct s. Let D := {s ∈ ℝ : μ_C(L_s) > 0}. For n ≥ 1, let D_n := {s : μ_C(L_s) > 1/n}. If s_1, …, s_m are distinct elements of D_n, then m/n < Σ_i μ_C(L_{s_i}) = μ_C(⋃_i L_{s_i}) ≤ μ_C(ℝ^P) = μ(C) < ∞. So D_n has at most n·μ(C) elements, and D = ⋃_{n≥1} D_n is countable. (In Mathlib this is `MeasureTheory.Measure.countable_meas_level_set_pos` applied to `hg.measurable` and the finite, hence s-finite, measure `μ.restrict (tsupport g)`. Register `IsFiniteMeasure (μ.restrict (tsupport g))` from `Measure.restrict_apply_univ` and μ(C) < ∞.)
3. Choice of t. A countable subset of ℝ is Lebesgue-null (`Set.Countable.measure_zero`). So Lebesgue-a.e. t ∈ ℝ satisfies t ∉ D (`measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem`), and the same then holds a.e. for Lebesgue measure restricted to (0, ∞) (`ae_restrict_of_ae`). Also, a.e. point for that restricted measure lies in (0, ∞) (`ae_restrict_mem measurableSet_Ioi`). Fix t with t > 0 and t ∉ D. It suffices to show μ_j(G) → μ(G) in [0, ∞], where G := {x : g(x) > t}. This gives the claim for every t outside a null set.
4. Topology of the superlevel sets. Let K := {x : g(x) ≥ t}. If x ∈ K, then g(x) ≥ t > 0, so g(x) ≠ 0 and x ∈ support g ⊆ C. Hence G ⊆ K ⊆ C ⊆ U. Because g is continuous, G = g⁻¹((t, ∞)) is open and K = g⁻¹([t, ∞)) is closed (`isOpen_lt continuous_const hg`, `isClosed_le continuous_const hg`). As a closed subset of the compact set C, K is compact (`IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset`).
5. μ(K) = μ(G). We have K ∖ G = {x : g(x) = t} = L_t, and L_t ⊆ K ⊆ C. So μ(K ∖ G) = μ(L_t) = μ(L_t ∩ C) = μ_C(L_t) (`Measure.restrict_eq_self`), and μ_C(L_t) = 0 because t ∉ D. Since K = G ∪ (K ∖ G) (`union_sdiff_cancel`), subadditivity (`measure_union_le`) gives μ(K) ≤ μ(G) + μ(K ∖ G) = μ(G). Monotonicity gives μ(G) ≤ μ(K). Hence μ(K) = μ(G). (Alternatively, Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.meas_le_ae_eq_meas_lt` gives μ{g ≥ t} = μ{g > t} for a.e. t by a different route.)
6. Squeeze. By (c) for the open set G ⊆ U, μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G). Since μ_j(G) ≤ μ_j(K) for every j, we get limsup_j μ_j(G) ≤ limsup_j μ_j(K) (`limsup_le_limsup`). By (b) for the compact set K ⊆ U, limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) = μ(G). Hence limsup_j μ_j(G) ≤ μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G). In [0, ∞], a complete linear order with the order topology in which every sequence is bounded, this forces μ_j(G) → μ(G) (`tendsto_of_le_liminf_of_limsup_le hinf hsup`; with `exact`/`refine` the boundedness auto-parameters close by themselves).
7. By steps 3–6, μ_j({g > t}) → μ({g > t}) for a.e. t with respect to Lebesgue measure restricted to (0, ∞). ∎
Implementation note: once μ(K ∖ G) = 0 is known, Mathlib's Portmanteau lemma `MeasureTheory.tendsto_measure_of_le_liminf_measure_of_limsup_measure_le` would also give step 6 (and the conclusion μ(K) = μ(G) of step 5), but `Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Portmanteau` is not in the import closure of `GMT.Ch07.Submission`. The direct squeeze above uses only imported lemmas.
proof_key_steps: C := tsupport g is compact and ⊆ U, so μ(C) < ∞ by (a); μ⌞C is a finite measure.
The level sets {g = s} are disjoint Borel sets, so only countably many have positive μ⌞C-measure. Hence for Lebesgue-a.e. t > 0, μ({g = t}) = 0.
For such t > 0: G = {g > t} is open, K = {g ≥ t} is compact, G ⊆ K ⊆ C ⊆ U, and μ(K) = μ(G) because K ∖ G = {g = t}.
limsup_j μ_j(G) ≤ limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) = μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G) by (b) and (c), so μ_j(G) → μ(G) in [0, ∞].

subproblems.title: Convergence of integrals of a nonnegative test function from a.e. convergence of its distribution function
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ, μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) be Borel measures on ℝ^P, and let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be continuous, nonnegative and compactly supported, with μ(tsupport g) < ∞ and limsup_j μ_j(tsupport g) < ∞ (lim sup in [0, ∞]), where tsupport g := closure{x : g(x) ≠ 0}. Suppose that for almost every t ∈ (0, ∞) with respect to Lebesgue measure restricted to (0, ∞), μ_j({x : g(x) > t}) → μ({x : g(x) > t}) in [0, ∞]. Then ∫ g dμ_j → ∫ g dμ (Bochner integrals).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid P → ℝ), Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → (∀ x, 0 ≤ g x) → μ (tsupport g) < ∞ → limsup (fun j => μs j (tsupport g)) atTop < ∞ → (∀ᵐ t ∂(volume.restrict (Ioi (0 : ℝ))), Tendsto (fun j => μs j {x | t < g x}) atTop (𝓝 (μ {x | t < g x}))) → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ x, g x ∂(μs j)) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, g x ∂μ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 2 (the bound b and g ≥ 0), 3 and 5 of the parent proof of `cmc_tendsto_integral_of_limsup_liminf` (the "standard approximation argument" that ends Simon's proof of 7.2.4, chapter-07.txt lines 284–289). The level-set convergence of step 4 is taken here as a hypothesis.
1. Notation and boundedness. Let C := tsupport g, a compact set containing support g. A continuous function with compact support is bounded, so there is b ∈ ℝ with |g(x)| ≤ b, hence g(x) ≤ b, for all x (`Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support`, then `Real.le_norm_self`).
2. Eventual uniform bound on μ_j(C). Since limsup_j μ_j(C) < ∞, there is Λ ∈ [0, ∞] with limsup_j μ_j(C) < Λ < ∞ (`exists_between`). Then μ_j(C) < Λ for all large j (`eventually_lt_of_limsup_lt`): there is j₀ with μ_j(C) < Λ for all j ≥ j₀. Let Λ' := Λ.toReal, a real number ≥ 0.
3. Integrability. Let ν be any Borel measure on ℝ^P with ν(C) < ∞. The restriction ν⌞C is a finite measure (its total mass is ν(C), by `Measure.restrict_apply_univ`), hence finite on compact sets. So the continuous compactly supported function g is ν⌞C-integrable (`Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport`). Since support g ⊆ C, this means g is ν-integrable (`integrableOn_iff_integrable_of_support_subset (subset_tsupport g)`). This applies to ν = μ, since μ(C) < ∞ by hypothesis, and to ν = μ_j for every j ≥ j₀, since μ_j(C) < Λ < ∞.
4. Layer cake (Cavalieri). For every ν as in step 3, g ≥ 0 is ν-integrable, so ∫ g dν = ∫_{(0,∞)} ν({g > t}) dt, with ν({g > t}) read as a real number. This is `Integrable.integral_eq_integral_meas_lt`, whose right side is `∫ t in Ioi 0, ν.real {x | t < g x}`.
5. The distribution functions. For a measure ν let F_ν(t) := ν({g > t}).toReal for t ∈ ℝ. The map t ↦ ν({g > t}) ∈ [0, ∞] is antitone, because {g > t} shrinks as t grows. So it is Borel measurable (`Antitone.measurable`), F_ν is measurable (`Measurable.ennreal_toReal`), and in particular F_ν is a.e.-strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to (0, ∞). Write F_j := F_{μ_j} and F := F_μ.
6. Two facts about superlevel sets. (i) If t > 0, then {g > t} ⊆ support g ⊆ C, since g(x) > t > 0 implies g(x) ≠ 0. (ii) If t ≥ b, then {g > t} = ∅, since g ≤ b.
7. Domination. Let h := Λ'·1_{(−∞, b]}, i.e. h(t) = Λ' for t ≤ b and h(t) = 0 otherwise. Take j ≥ j₀ and t > 0. If t ≤ b, then by 6(i) and step 2, μ_j({g > t}) ≤ μ_j(C) < Λ < ∞, so 0 ≤ F_j(t) ≤ Λ' = h(t) (`ENNReal.toReal_mono`). If t > b, then by 6(ii), F_j(t) = 0 = h(t). Hence |F_j(t)| ≤ h(t) for all t ∈ (0, ∞) and all j ≥ j₀. The function h is integrable for Lebesgue measure restricted to (0, ∞): it is a constant times the indicator of the measurable set (−∞, b], and that set has restricted measure Leb((−∞, b] ∩ (0, ∞)) ≤ Leb([0, b]) < ∞ (`integrable_indicator_iff measurableSet_Iic`, `integrableOn_const`, `Measure.restrict_apply`, `measure_Icc_lt_top`).
8. Pointwise convergence a.e. By hypothesis, μ_j({g > t}) → μ({g > t}) in [0, ∞] for a.e. t ∈ (0, ∞) (Lebesgue). For such t we also have t > 0, so μ({g > t}) ≤ μ(C) < ∞ by 6(i). Since toReal is continuous at every finite point of [0, ∞] (`ENNReal.tendsto_toReal`), F_j(t) → F(t).
9. Dominated convergence. Apply the dominated convergence theorem along the filter atTop on ℕ, where the bound only needs to hold for j ≥ j₀ (`tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence`), using steps 5, 7 and 8. This gives ∫_{(0,∞)} F_j(t) dt → ∫_{(0,∞)} F(t) dt.
10. Conclusion. By step 4, ∫_{(0,∞)} F(t) dt = ∫ g dμ, and ∫_{(0,∞)} F_j(t) dt = ∫ g dμ_j for every j ≥ j₀. A sequence that agrees with a convergent sequence for all large indices has the same limit (`Tendsto.congr'`). So ∫ g dμ_j → ∫ g dμ. ∎
proof_key_steps: g ≤ b for some b ∈ ℝ. Choose Λ with limsup_j μ_j(tsupport g) < Λ < ∞, so μ_j(tsupport g) < Λ for j ≥ j₀.
g is integrable for every ν with ν(tsupport g) < ∞: μ and μ_j for j ≥ j₀.
Layer cake: ∫ g dν = ∫_{(0,∞)} ν({g > t}) dt for these ν.
For j ≥ j₀ the integrands are dominated by Λ'·1_{t ≤ b}, which is integrable on (0, ∞), and they converge a.e. because μ({g > t}) ≤ μ(tsupport g) < ∞.
Dominated convergence along atTop, plus agreement of the two sequences for j ≥ j₀, gives ∫ g dμ_j → ∫ g dμ.
